source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Cincinnati CIN2 campus publishes 11 MW of IT capacity and 143,778 square feet of technical space, making it one of only nine Ohio facilities that disclose a megawatt figure at all.

The disclosed number is the input, not the answer. The operator publishes no rack count, no accelerator count, and no power density, so any conversion to racks is an outside assumption. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 11 MW is roughly 275 racks. At 10 kW per rack it is about 1,100. The same 11 MW supports very different amounts of compute depending on a figure CyrusOne has not published.

The certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, and SSAE 16 Type II, qualify the building for regulated workloads rather than AI workloads specifically. They say what kinds of data the campus is permitted to hold, not who holds it. No tenant names are published.

Ohio maps 79 facilities, of which 9 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 118.4 MW. CIN2's 11 MW ranks fourth among those nine. The gap between 79 and 9 is the real finding: the state total reflects only what operators chose to disclose, so it is a floor and not a census. CIN2 is a mid-sized entry within a small disclosed set, and nothing here establishes how much of its load serves AI rather than ordinary enterprise colocation.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
